title: Every exit-21 and exit-1 cause has a machine-readable code

record.title: Every exit-21 and exit-1 cause has a machine-readable code
record.requirement: every cause of exit 21 (not running, unwrapped name, strict-modes, server verification, endpoint lost mid-call) and of exit 1 (already live, stale heartbeat, squatted name, pinned-hash mismatch, script child, strict-modes or socket-directory refusal, internal error) reaches `--json`, MCP and the process log as a distinct code with no path or pid, matching the human hint for the same cause.
record.observed_gap: exit 21 and exit 1 each have several causes; design now gives one hint per cause in human mode, but arch fixes `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` for exit 21 and gives exit 1 no `--json` document (A:292-294; DS cli pattern 2 "pending an arch amendment"); obs's codes lack stale heartbeat and unwrapped name (OB §6 detail code catalog, D-20), and strict-modes or socket-directory refusals at `run`/`ui`/`mcp` start have no code (XF X7, T4, F4, B6).

verification.acceptance: Each cause reaches its own closed code on each surface it reaches, carrying no path or pid and matching the human hint of that cause. Exit 21: strict-modes-failed, instance-dead (not running), unwrapped-name, endpoint-lost and server-verify-failed, printed in detail under --json as {"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"} and returned by MCP as the same body less v, its text refused: instance-unreachable; on the process log as the process-exit detail of each cause a log is open for, exit 21 at WARN, endpoint-lost with during call. Exit 1, in the error of {"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null} on revive --json and the catch site under --json, and in the process-exit detail: strict-modes-failed, already-live, no-session, session-live, cwd-missing, stale-heartbeat, batch-script-child, pinned-hash-mismatch, squatted-name, internal-error; verify's refusals on the process-exit it writes under a VIOLA_NAME: program-not-found, version-unreadable, unclean-fixture, pinned-hash-mismatch, batch-script-child, strict-modes-failed, interrupted. Each human form ends stderr with that cause's own hint: line (internal-error none), and no hint two codes share (tests/cross_exit_causes.rs no_two_codes_share_a_hint beside its planted-duplicate control shared_hints_reads_a_planted_duplicate). Witnesses: tests/cross_exit_causes.rs, crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs, tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs, tests/cli_instance_state.rs, tests/cli_verify.rs. Named apart, on the founder's own word (chunks/2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue/inputs/I2-relay-1.md.txt Q4): a strict-modes check refused before a log opens writes no line; MCP reaches only the exit-21 causes its five tools can meet and writes no line, isError its record; run and verify have no --json, so their causes reach the log and the hint, run's start also through revive --json; viola mcp's own exit 1 keeps both streams empty; macOS's server check and the socket-directory refusal stay with the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening".

title: CLI contract: machine output, typed exits, cause-named hints

record.title: CLI contract: machine output, typed exits, cause-named hints
record.requirement: every verb has a `--json` form mirroring the channel result and a typed exit code (0, 1, 2, 10–14, 20, 21); human output follows the design phraseology (readback mirror for `send`, one `hint:` naming the next step per cause, results on stdout and context on stderr); a global `--home` isolates all state; `config.json` sets thresholds, port and diagnostics level, and no setting can switch off a security control.
record.observed_gap: the prototype prints free text; drivers need parseable refusals (A:98).

verification.acceptance: Every driver-facing verb (send, wait, last, answer, list, pause, release, and revive with --list) has a --json form printing one stdout document that mirrors the channel result, or the documented error form where none exists ({"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault",…}, instance-unreachable's detail its closed cause, and revive's exit-1 {"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null} with the code one of strict-modes-failed, already-live, stale-heartbeat, no-session, session-live, cwd-missing, batch-script-child, pinned-hash-mismatch, squatted-name, internal-error, each refusal of the start revive shares with run included: one document, exit 1, stderr empty). Stderr is empty and the exit is typed from {0, 1, 2, 10-14, 20, 21}, read side by side per outcome in tests/cli_machine_contract.rs and the landed per-verb cases it names. In human mode, results go to stdout and context to stderr, each refusal cause ends stderr with its own hint: line, no hint names release, and send prints its readback mirror (the landed literal pins in tests/cli_send.rs, tests/cli_wheel.rs, tests/cli_revive.rs, tests/cli_list.rs and the trycmd mirror). A global --home isolates all state (the two-home case in tests/cli_machine_contract.rs). The home resolves --home, then the VIOLA_DIR grandparent through the one shape check, then the default, and is canonicalised once it exists. config.json sets the budget thresholds and the diagnostics level, and no config.json key, global flag or VIOLA_* variable switches off a control (the completeness case in tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs over schemas/config.v1.json). The port clause left 0.1.0 by the founder's 2026-10-16 ruling (this capability's notes).

title: Hooks report normalised events and fail open

record.title: Hooks report normalised events and fail open
record.requirement: every registered hook event becomes one normalised event line in the instance's log (never a raw Claude payload); harness-injected prompts are classified as harness, long-paste wrappers and tag escaping are normalised away; a hook outside a wrapped session is a silent no-op that writes nothing anywhere; any hook failure exits 0 with no output so the human sees the dialog; spine hooks never delay a turn past their deadline.
record.observed_gap: the prototype's hooks fire with the wrapper's identity (B §4.1 S2); the product has none.

verification.acceptance: In root integration tests on all three CI OSes (tests/hook_events.rs, tests/hook_fail_open.rs): each of the seven registered hook events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd, Notification, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure), fired by the fake agent through a live `viola run` wrapper, yields exactly one events.ndjson line of its normalised kind with source "hook" whose data keys equal that kind's literal set and carry no raw payload key; a `<task-notification>` or `<agent-message from=` prefixed prompt yields origin "harness"; the CLI's unescaped long-paste pair (`<pasted_content id="X">` ... `</pasted_content id="X">`) is unwrapped and typed escaped tag text (`<\pasted_content`, `<\/pasted_content`) is un-escaped and never unwrapped; `viola hook` with no VIOLA_NAME exits 0 and creates no diagnostics/ or instances/ dir; every fail-open case (oversize stdin, malformed JSON, clap error incl. --help, unknown event, unreachable endpoint, no snapshot, VIOLA_NAME absent or invalid) exits 0 with empty stdout and stderr within the 1.0 s provisional spine bound, below which the hook enforces its own 750 ms deadline. A panic in the hook maps to exit 0, proven in-process (catch-site table + panic-line writer); the forced panic on the real binary and the worst-sample hyperfine proof belong to the Hook perf gate entry. The dialog tier's "the human sees the dialog" half applies from the dialog chunk (:62).

title: `send` types at a turn boundary and is confirmed after the fact

record.title: `send` types at a turn boundary and is confirmed after the fact
record.requirement: a driver's text (from stdin or a file, never a leading-slash argument, with a warning on a rewritten path) is typed as one paste plus Enter only when the input box is ready; it returns read back only when the matching prompt is seen, `not-delivered` with a typed detail otherwise (`input-not-ready`, `no-prompt-submitted`, `turn-running`, `control-character`), and `unconfirmable` only for a ledger-listed local command without a measured post-condition; `/clear` is confirmed by its new-session post-condition; text with a disallowed control character is refused, never stripped.
record.observed_gap: the prototype sends without a readiness gate; a CLI-native modal swallowed a paste (M1), local commands fire no prompt event (M5), and Git Bash rewrote a leading-slash argument (B §6).

on a verified CLI it is typed only when the input box is ready (`send_on_a_verified_cli_refuses_while_the_trust_dialog_is_up`); otherwise it returns not-delivered with a typed detail: input not ready (the same case), no prompt submitted (`send_window_no_prompt_submitted_refuses_and_logs`), turn running (`send_window_second_concurrent_send_is_refused_turn_running`, `send_after_a_confirmed_send_is_turn_running_until_turn_ended`), control character (`setting_does_not_disable_the_send_paste_control`, `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`, and the unit table `send_refusal_order`); title: `wait` and `last` wake on turn boundaries without polling

record.title: `wait` and `last` wake on turn boundaries without polling
record.requirement: `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event (turn ended, question, permission, plan, session end) at or after a cursor — at once if it is already logged, never woken by activity, wheel, budget or send-record lines — times out with a typed result, reports an unreachable instance when the wrapper vanishes, and `last` returns the newest turn's final text; every send and wait result carries the cursor for the next call.
record.observed_gap: the prototype's `wait` exits on the next Stop (B §4.1 S5); there is no cursor-based contract.

verification.acceptance: wait returns the first driver-relevant event at or after the given cursor, at once if already logged, and is never woken by activity, wheel, budget-gate or send-record lines: end to end on all three CI OSes for turn-ended — path3_wait_parks_until_turn_ended_then_last_reads_it (a viola wait --after C stays parked across an activity line, returns turn-ended with cursor equal to that line's end offset, and the same --after is answered at once) and wait_after_a_send_cursor_returns_the_turn (a send ok cursor is a valid after); the full five-kind wake set (turn-ended, question, permission, plan, session-end) against every other kind, an unknown one included, by the run::wait::tests clock-driven unit table. It times out with {"v":1,"ok":{"timed_out":true}} at exit 0 (path3, --timeout-ms 500), and only once the injected clock passes timeout_ms (unit). It reports instance-unreachable, exit 21 {"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}, when the wrapper is killed while it is parked (chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21, during:"call"). last returns the newest turn-ended's last_assistant_message and ts, null/null before any turn, unchanged across a wrapper restart (last_survives_a_wrapper_restart). Every send ok and wait event result carries the cursor for the next call. The dialog kinds' end-to-end wait witness is owed to working-route.md:78 (the operator's condition at this claim).

title: Dialogs answered through hooks by `dialog_id`

record.title: Dialogs answered through hooks by `dialog_id`
record.requirement: exactly one dialog is pending per instance and appears once in the log with its id; a driver answers a question (option or free text, with notes), a permission (allow, or deny with a message, plus a suggestion if F-16 admits one) or a plan (approve, or revise with a message) and the dialog never renders; a second concurrent dialog, a human wheel, an unverified CLI or an expired deadline all leave the dialog to the human; an unknown id is refused `unknown-dialog`.
record.observed_gap: the prototype answers questions (including free text and annotations), permissions and plans through hooks (B §4.1 S3, S7, S8).

Proved in two parts. (1) Every clause but "never renders", under the fake agent on the three CI OSes: the `path4_*` cases of `tests/cli_answer.rs` (logged once, woken and answered by id for a question, a permission and a plan; a second concurrent dialog; an unstamped home; a stamp failing the dialog rows), `path4_a_dialog_pending_at_a_pause_is_handed_back_to_the_human` and the pause case of `tests/cli_wheel.rs`, and `hook_dialog_expires_at_the_deadline_on_the_injected_clock` and `hook_dialog_under_a_human_wheel_is_logged_once_and_null_at_once` in `src/run/dialog.rs`; no permission suggestion is admitted in v1. (2) "Never renders", on live `claude` 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host, through the product binary: each of the three kinds (a question, a permission answered deny, a plan) is raised in one `viola run` session and decided by a driver through `viola answer` by its id inside the deadline; for each, `dialog-raised`, `dialog-answered` and a `hook-decision` with `decision_emitted:true` and `deadline_hit:false` share its `dialog_id`, and its turn reaches `turn-ended` with no `wheel` record and no key typed into the session, with nobody at the desk (chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive, `evidence/live-run.ndjson`, the three `dialog-*` step lines; its run reader gate requires all three). The reading is of the effect on the product's records, not of screen content. A kind the live CLI does not raise leaves this acceptance unmet.

body: - OPEN — whether the real `claude` on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize · owner: the measurement of the route entry «Key after a resize» (0.2.0, Epoch 4)

- **[Real-time Strategy]** viola has no web or graphical frontend. Its view beyond `viola list` is the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14), owed by the 0.2.0 Epoch 6 route entries «Console scaffold», «Fleet console view» and «Console actions».

- **[GUI Control Scope]** No page and no graphical control surface: the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) is the one view beyond `viola list`, and what it shows is the route entry «Fleet console view»'s to name.

- **[Deferred] Deferred to specialists and later versions:** auth generally (security, v1.x); the test framework, fake-agent harness and `viola verify` probe design (tests); logging and observability (obs); self-update, signing and a marketplace entry (later version).
**GUI contracts.** None: viola has no web or graphical surface; the terminal fleet console's contracts (matrix#v2-14) are owed by the route entry «Console scaffold».

- **Scale path.**
  - v1 is personal and Linux only (first live on the Linux dev host, by the founder's ruling R-L1; CI-tested on `ubuntu-latest` against the fake agent; the Windows and macOS code recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`).
  - v1.x adds public distribution (dist 0.33.0 releases, signing, a marketplace entry, self_update 1.3.0).
  - A phone or remote view comes later, behind authentication.

- Code-graph planes (`scripts/code-graph.py`, one DuckDB per language plane under `.andromeda/cache/{plane}/`):
  - **rust:** the root workspace through rust-analyzer SCIP. It indexes every member (`viola`, `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`, `viola-agent-claude`, `viola-state`, `viola-mcp`, `viola-e2e`). `fuzz/`, a separate workspace, is outside it.
  - **ts:** none: the tree tracks no `tsconfig.json`, so `scripts/code-graph.py` detects no ts plane.

- **Approach:** none for v1 (as of 2026-09-23). The only principal is the local OS user.
  - Reason: Project Intent and Established Decisions (Personal v1) describe a single-user local tool with "no accounts, no hosting".
  - Access control therefore depends entirely on OS-level isolation: who can connect to each IPC endpoint and who can read or write `~/.viola/`. Cross-cutting Patterns (Local endpoint trust boundary) sets the target principal as "every process of the same OS user and no other".
  - The enforcement mechanism for that boundary is this specialist's: Authentication & Authorization sets it, enforced on Linux, the one target.
- dist `>=0.33.0` with GitHub Artifact Attestations.
- From v1.x: the zipsign private key (self_update `signatures`), held only as a CI secret in the release workflow.
No web surface: viola renders no page. The keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14) takes its own surface section at the route entry «Console scaffold».

- **Line form (stderr):** `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>`, fields separated by two spaces. `viola send` pads `unable` into the mirror's word column after `[/ ]`. The fixed-message exceptions are the exit-1 start refusals of `viola run` (`unable: <name> is already live` and its sibling causes, listed in design-system cli pattern 2), the exit-1 refusals of `viola revive` (the same collision pair, and its own five pairs under Output structure — `viola revive`; under `--json` its `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document in place of the pair) and `viola verify`'s exit-1 refusals, each an `unable: <text>` line and its own `hint:` line with no name, path or pid: `the claude CLI was not found` / `install Claude Code or put it on PATH`; `the CLI version could not be read` / `run claude --version to check the install`; `a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>` (a screen fixture: `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>`; codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`; it names the fixture file and the check, never the content) / `record with a viola home under your user home`; `verify was stopped before it finished` / `run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` (a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM, stdout empty); `the viola home is not private to you` / `the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (the home pair: its strict-modes check refuses the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its log opens, or refuses the stamps write; stdout empty, no step line, no summary); plus run's pinned-copy refusal; and the home-tree refusal of the `viola run` and `viola revive` starts, checked before the wrapper log opens: the home pair for the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/` or the pinned copy's folders and file, `revive`'s instance pair for the instance's state files, no log opened, no line, no child; and the socket-directory refusal of the `viola run` and `viola revive` starts, exit 1, made before any snapshot, child or bind, stdout empty and the directory left as found: `unable: the socket directory for <name> cannot be trusted` / `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (under `revive --json` its document, Output structure — `viola revive`); and `viola list`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the whole board (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, the operator's answer superseded 2026-10-13), stdout empty: `unable: the viola home is not private to you` / `hint: the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` for the home or `instances/`, and `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only` (`revive`'s pair) for one instance; and `viola plugin install`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal, stdout empty, the same home pair for the home or a `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created and no log opened; and the exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the frame verbs `viola send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (for these two `<name>` is the driven instance), made before any role file or log opens, stdout empty: `revive`'s instance pair (`unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`), no line written to any log and the directory's mode left as found; under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` with stderr empty. A failed or panicked `cli` verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `verify`, `revive --list`, `plugin install`, `link`, `unlink`; a `revive` start stays outside it) prints exactly `error: internal error` once, from the one catch site, with no hint, and with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout in its place with stderr empty (for `wait` / `last` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply, an unparseable reply or any other channel error; for `link` / `unlink` a refusal reply or an `ok` of another shape; for `list` an `instances/` that cannot be listed and a log start that fails, while a per-instance read error gives no row).

- **Hint line:** directly under each refusal, `hint: <one plain instruction>`, keyed by reason (or by reason · detail). Exit 21 and exit 1 each have several causes, and every cause gets its own hint, so an agent can tell the causes apart from the last stderr line (design-system cli pattern 2). The exit-1 start refusal `unable: <name> is already live` takes `hint: viola list`. `wait`, `last`, `link` and `unlink`'s exit 21 `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` (for `link` / `unlink`, `<name>` is the driven instance) takes `hint: <name> is not running; viola list shows the live instances` when the instance is not running (`viola send`'s exit 21 keeps its `[/ ] unable` mirror with the same hint). A frame verb's exit 21 on a name with no directory at its instance path takes `hint: <name> is not a wrapped session; only sessions started with viola run take commands`, and with its wrapper lost while the call is open `hint: <name>'s wrapper went away during the call; viola list shows whether it is still running`, each the last stderr line in plain ASCII. A frame verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) whose server check finds that the process on the endpoint is not the recorded wrapper, or cannot make the check, writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` with stderr empty. A frame verb meeting a refused socket directory writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` with stderr empty. There is no hint for the `unknown` refusal, whose detail is a code word or nothing, for `wrapper fault` or for `internal error`. A hint never quotes the sent text or any upstream text, and never names a path or a pid.

- **Flat verbs:** one lower-case word each (`plugin install` is the one two-word verb). There is no nested noun hierarchy, no interactive prompt and no pager in a verb; the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) is no verb's output, and its own surface is owed by the route entry «Console scaffold».

- **Shared vocabulary:**
  - The six captions, words and slot order are fixed, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) reuses them.
  - The readback vocabulary is `open`, `read back`, `unable`, `unconfirmable`. The CLI brackets the box.
  - ` - ` separates inside a CLI field, and an arrow is `->`. There is no CLI inbound `<-` form.
  - Amber means `DIALOG` and nothing else. `stale` is SGR dim in the terminal.
  - The CLI is where every action lives.

Inherited pattern: arch excerpt, Test Harness Commitment ("Development Style: agent-driven") with harness design deferred to tests. Binding founder direction: creator excerpt, Founder Directions 2 and 3: "the fake agent + `viola verify` fixtures are the contract"; "Structured JSON logs from every process (run/hook/mcp) … a `logs` command in the harness, hook trace in diagnostics/".

- **Trigger type:** cross-surface-coordination
  - **Source:** design excerpt, Layout Categories (the fixed captions and slot order of CLI `viola list`); creator excerpt, Founder Direction 5 (CL-1 `send-issued` / `send-refused`)
  - **Required test type:**
    - a `send` shows `[RB]` on the CLI
    - `send-refused` shows `[/ ]` / exit 10–14
    - MCP and CLI return identical `ok` / refusal payloads for the same channel result

- **Session record:** each harness session writes `target/agent-run/<session>/session.json` with `{v, session, home, instances:[{name, wrapper_pid, started_at, fake_args}], supervisor_pid, supervisor_started_at, agents_mode}`; `agents_mode` (`recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed`, serde default `recorded`, by chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs) is written by `boot` and stands in `supervise.json` too. `viola-e2e` holds no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an older record lacking `agents_mode` still parses. The default session is `default`, and `--session <id>` allows parallel sessions.
N/A — viola has no web or graphical frontend.

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh run [--unit|--integration|--e2e|--mutants|--coverage|--perf|--fuzz-replay|--all] [--filter <nextest-filterset>] [--file <path>]... [--package <member>] [--local-live]`. `--file` (repeatable) needs `--mutants` (clap `requires`): it scopes the mutation run to those sources, the inner fix-loop (step 4). `--package` also needs `--mutants`: it mutates one whole member, the boundary tier's form (step 4 Package). `--coverage`, `--fuzz-replay` and `--mutants` never join the default selection. With no selector and no `--local-live` the default is `--all`, which runs steps 1 and 2 in order (`--local-live` passed alone is a selection of its own and runs neither step); step 4 runs only under `--mutants`:
  1. Unit + integration: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E '<layer filterset>'`, then `cargo test --workspace --doc`, both with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<workspace root>/target/harness` (boot step 1). JUnit is still read from `<workspace root>/target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`: nextest's store is workspace-root-relative whatever the target dir (measured 2026-09-24). The layer filtersets are:
     - unit: `kind(lib) | kind(bin)`
     - integration: `kind(test) & !binary(/^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)`, the complement of step 2's layer, so a test binary reports in exactly one of the two. A `binary()` regex that matches no binary is a nextest filterset parse error, not an empty set (as measured on cargo-nextest 0.9.146 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: a scratch crate, exit 94 "operator didn't match any binary names"; first measured on 0.9.133, 2026-09-24); the regex matches the root `chaos_`, `contract_`, `cross_`, `tui_` and `path<N>_` binaries, so both layers parse in this workspace, and the harness's own throwaway-workspace cases plant one `path_` binary before an integration run.
  2. Fake-agent E2E: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E 'binary(/^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)'`, suite `nextest-e2e`, run third after step 1's two nextest runs (`run --e2e`; in the default and `--all`), through the same nextest shape and target dir, a `--filter` intersecting it. `[0-9]*` after `path` admits the numbered Path binaries (`path1_run_start`, `path6_budget_harness`), which the written `^(path|…)_` did not select (as measured at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: 18 binaries, and `run --integration` ran `path1`). 20 binaries / 157 tests at that chunk's end. `run --e2e` alone runs no doctest (doctest stays with step 1 and `--coverage`); the run-archive list is unchanged (unit, integration and coverage JUnit). Every nextest test uses one boot model:
     - No test shells out to `agent-run` / `viola-harness`, so there is never a nested `cargo run` inside nextest.
     - Root `tests/` suites use the rstest chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`.
     - `crates/viola-e2e` scenarios use one of two boot models, chosen by the scenario's §6 Cleanup line:
       - Cleanup "harness `cleanup`" (Paths 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, E3): `viola_e2e::harness::session::harness_session(test, label, opts) -> HarnessSession`, a plain function and drop guard (`viola-e2e` carries no `[dev-dependencies]`, so never an rstest fixture), landed at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs. It calls the same library code as the `boot` / `cleanup` commands (`viola_e2e::harness::{boot, cleanup}`) with `stamp: !opts.unstamped` (`SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, so the default session is stamped — the in-test form of `boot --unstamped`, chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, whose Path 7 MCP leg boots the default `overseer` + `builder` pair unstamped, `SessionOptions { unstamped: true, ..SessionOptions::default() }`), and the library `boot` spawns the `supervise` process from the given binary dir, so `cleanup`'s pid + start-time proof stays exact (fork 2 of that chunk, `inputs#I1`). `SessionOptions` defaults to `overseer` + `builder`, no `--statusline-echo`, `--agents-mode recorded`, stamped (`unstamped` false); the guard exposes `home()`, `instance_dir(name)`, `bin_dir()`, `session()`, `workspace()` and `cleanup(self)`, panics with the boot document unless ready, and never shells out to `agent-run`. Its `Drop` runs `cleanup` (the home kept) unless `cleanup(self)` ran, then removes the home's parent unless `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, or `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` while the test is panicking. `harness_session` always skips boot step 1, so no `cargo build` runs inside nextest. It passes `viola_e2e::harness::boot` the binary dir found from the test executable's own target dir, never a literal `target/<profile>`, and boot step 3 copies the fake agent from that same dir. This is the same binary-dir parameter `--perf` uses (§10). As a result, the scenarios spawn the instrumented `viola` / `viola-fake-agent` under `--coverage`, and the plain debug binaries otherwise.
       - Cleanup "TempDir drop" or a test-owned outer PTY (Paths 1, 5, E1, E2, E5): the chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper` from `viola_e2e::fixtures`. Root `tests/support/` cannot be imported by another package, and the root package must not dev-depend on the tokio-based `viola-e2e`, so the chain exists twice (the sync root copy and the `viola-e2e` copy) against one contract. In both copies `stamped_home` runs `viola verify` against the fake agent. Today only the sync root copy exists (`tests/support/home.rs`; homes under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*`). The `viola_e2e::fixtures` copy lands with its first consumer among these scenarios; Path 1's flow is not one, landing on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs` (fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs, `inputs#I1`). The root `stamped_home` runs `viola --home <h> verify -- <fake agent> --cli-version 2.1.287 --fixtures <root>/fixtures/claude` (the committed recorded set; `2.1.287` is the root chain's one literal, `tests/support/fake.rs` `RECORDED_CLI_VERSION`), and `stamped` is true only on exit 0 and a last line `stamped 2.1.287  <n> pass  0 fail`; anything else panics with the exit and match codes. `StampedHome::unstamped(TestHome)` (`stamped:false`, writes nothing) serves the tests that assert the unverified path. `booted_wrapper` drives the wrapper through a test-owned outer PTY (`tests/support/outer_pty.rs`; `Wrapper::boot/send/stop` in `tests/support/home.rs`, and `tests/run_cli.rs::run_viola`) and waits for `process-start` lines for `self` and `claude-child` and a fake-agent `start` receipt, each newer than the boot (a `gone` name's files are reused) — the receipt means its terminal is raw, so no key sent after it is swallowed — then for the snapshot (`pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid`) and a heartbeat under 5 s, bounded at 7 s — `WITHIN` in `tests/support/watch.rs`, shared by the root waits on a child (`Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 31 sites in 23 files under `tests/` (`grep -rn 'Instant::now() + WITHIN' tests/ | wc -l` and `grep -rln 'Instant::now() + WITHIN' tests/ | wc -l`), as measured at chunk 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci's wrap on the Linux dev host; architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem states the count's rule) and strictly below the nextest `mutants` profile's 10 s kill, so a stuck wait fails the test itself. `Wrapper::boot` always passes `--cli-version 2.1.287` (`--fixtures` stays a per-test extra). `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` wait for the wrapper's exit and then, when the snapshot recorded an `endpoint`, for that endpoint to be unconnectable (`wait_endpoint_gone`; `unconnectable` is the harness `endpoint_gone` rule — a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, what `holder_gone` reads). The kill path (`Wrapper::kill`, used by `tests/chaos_revive.rs`) kills the wrapper the test booted, waits for its exit, then for the child it recorded to be gone by pid and start time, then on `holder_gone` in place of `wait_endpoint_gone`: a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent. A killed wrapper removes nothing, so on Unix its socket file stays (the next bind takes over a leftover socket file) and a wait on the file being absent never ends after a kill (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive; the kill-and-revive case green on a run of the retired three-OS matrix). The stop path keeps the `unconnectable` rule. An exit code is not the endpoint gone. Each wait notes what it polls (codes, counts and booleans, read in the predicate's own short-circuit order) to `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test>.<label>.report`, one line per change, kept on a failure or a runner kill and removed on a pass. The wait is exit-aware: when `child.try_wait()` reports that the wrapper exited first, it fails at once (`wrapper <name> exited before ready`) instead of waiting out the bound. The bound stays below cargo-mutants' 20 s auto-timeout floor, so a mutant that stops the wrapper from getting ready grades as caught, not Timeout. Harness `boot` keeps its 20 s per-instance bound.
     - In §6, a step written `agent-run boot --session <id> <flags>` means `harness_session` with those flags. A Cleanup written `agent-run cleanup --session <id>` means harness `cleanup` as defined below. The `<id>` there (`p2`, `p7`) is only a readable label. The real session id always follows the `<test name>-<label>-<pid>` rule below, so neither parallel tests nor two sessions opened by one test (Path 7) share a session.
     - "Harness `cleanup`" means the test calls `session.cleanup()` at the end and asserts the report: no field `false` (an interim `null` field is allowed), same shape as the `cleanup` command. `Drop` is only a best-effort fallback for panicking tests.
     - The session id is `<test name>-<label>-<pid>`, where `<label>` is the §6 `--session` label (`p2`, `p7`, `p7-stamped`) or `main` when the step gives none. Each session gets its own temp home and its own `target/agent-run/<session>/` dir, because a session record holds exactly one `home`. The endpoint hash includes the absolute home, so the default `overseer` / `builder` names never collide across parallel tests.

When that commit is HEAD itself and the working tree's `.andromeda/master-route.md` holds no pending record HEAD's copy lacks (the wrap push, whose own commit is the flip), the base is `HEAD^`, so that push reads its own delta, never an empty diff. title: The live page sees a dialog clear and state refresh

record.requirement: the view learns, without polling, when a pending dialog clears and when liveness, status or the budget reading change, so the strip bay reflects current state through the same feed that carries events.

verification.acceptance: Without polling, an open page learns when a pending dialog clears and when liveness, status or the budget reading change, through the same feed that carries events, and the strip bay reflects the current state.

- **5-command requirements:**
  - `boot`:
    - Builds `viola` and creates a fresh temp home, passed as `--home` (arch excerpt, Per-test isolation).
    - Starts one or more `viola run <name> -- <fake agent> <args>` wrappers.
    - Readiness, per instance: `instances/<name>/snapshot.json` exists with `pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid` and `endpoint`. The `heartbeat` mtime is under 5 s old. The log has a start `wheel` and a `budget-gate` event, followed by `session-start` once "Verify-stamped test homes and harness" (the `boot` step-4 owner) joins it to harness readiness.
    - On readiness failure it exits non-zero with a JSON reason on stdout. A `run` refusal to start (exit 1: a `live` or `stale` name, or a tampered pinned copy) is surfaced verbatim.
  - `run`:
    - Invokes, in order:
      1. the workspace unit and integration tests (`cargo test`)
      2. fake-agent E2E against `fixtures/claude/*`
      3. none: viola has no browser suite, and the mutation step keeps its number 4
      4. mutation testing scoped to the chunk diff (Founder Direction 1: "surviving mutants are red") — only under `run --mutants`, never in the default or `--all`; its cadence is the epoch-boundary code audit
    - Exit 0 only if every suite passes and no mutant survives. Non-zero otherwise, with a JSON summary on stdout (suite, passed, failed, survived).
    - Local-only mode adds `viola verify` against the real CLI. It must never run in CI (arch excerpt, CI/CD).
  - `status`:
    - Queries `viola list --json --home <tmp>`.
    - The agent polls per item: `name`, `wrapped`, `liveness`, `status`, `wheel`, `budget_paused`, `dialog_pending`, `cli_verified`.
    - It also polls the envelope `skipped{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and `budget`.
  - `cleanup`:
    - Stops every wrapper started by `boot`. Exit is confirmed on the process handle, not EOF.
    - Deletes the temp home and verifies the endpoint is gone: a CLI verb against the name returns exit 21, and a connect to the socket path is refused or the path is absent; `cleanup` removes no leftover socket file, so a force-killed wrapper's file stays until a next bind of that name takes it over.
    - Must be idempotent: a second run exits 0 and reports nothing to clean.
  - `logs`:
    - Prints, as JSON lines, the structured per-process logs of `run` / `hook` / `mcp` / `cli` in the §3 log format (Founder Direction 3; the exact field set is not in the distilled excerpt, so Phase 3 pins it).

title: .claude/docs/gotchas.md

body:
**What breaks:** on the retired Windows runner (its code out of the tree, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) a key written into ConPTY right after `ResizePseudoConsole` returned was never read by the Rust test child, which was blocked in its console read (`ReadConsoleW` through Rust's stdin): measured 13 losses in 200 isolated iterations (6.5 %) of `spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code` under `cargo llvm-cov nextest` on `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260922.246.2 (ci#36527891850, job 109274838484). Every loss was class K: the child's size watcher saw the new size with no key, viola's writer had written and flushed the key, and ConPTY wrote no cursor-position request (`dsr-cpr 0`). The loss lies between the ConPTY input-pipe write and that test child's read; **where inside that span, and why, is not established** — an overseer read of microsoft/terminal's current source (relayed at the wrap, not verified here) found no input-buffer flush on the resize path and no reported resize input loss, so this is not recorded as a ConPTY defect. This host's conhost 10.0.26100.8875 read 20/20.
**The product window — open and unmeasured for `claude`:** viola forwards resizes and keys as they come and never holds, queues or reorders a human key behind a resize (a11y-plan §1), so nothing in viola closes this window. Whether the real `claude` (Node/libuv, reading with `ReadConsoleInputW`) loses a key typed right after a resize in `viola run` is **unmeasured**; the rate above is the Rust test child's. The open question is now whether the real `claude` on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize; owner: the measurement of the route entry «Key after a resize» (0.2.0, Epoch 4). The founder's product question on H2 stays open.
**How to avoid (tests only):** a test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first — the red test now waits for its watcher's `size 120x40` line, and read 200/200 under the same loop (ci#36529038462). That reshaped test does NOT cover the product window: it proves the key arrives once the resize has landed, not that a key racing a resize arrives, and it reads with the Rust child, never `claude`.
**Fix if broken:** read the kept reports in `<temp dir>/viola-pty-watch/` (`<test>.<pid>.report`, `<test>.<pid>.test.report`, `<pid>` the test process's id) by the chunk's localisation rule — class R (no `size` line), K (size seen, key flushed, key lost) or E (key before size) — before changing any wait; never raise `CHILD_WITHIN` or retry the test.
**With the sideloaded ConPTY** (removed with the Windows code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) (chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty`, one windows-2025 run, image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260828.587, ci#36563868040, the measurement-only race): sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe` 1.24.260710001 lost 0 of 200, the inbox ConPTY 14 of 200 — no rate claimed, and the product window above stays unmeasured for `claude`.
**References:** arch [PTY]; test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY, §10 Zero-flakiness budget; chunk `2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe` `evidence/h2-reproduction.md`; chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty` `evidence/h2-with-without.md`; microsoft/terminal PR #19535 (post-resize CPR — not seen on either build).

title: .claude/docs/design-summary.md

body: **"Strip-bay handoff, read back."** The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is an air-traffic-control tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks, and every session keeps its slot for life. The only warm light is the one amber arrival holder cocked out of line when a session needs you. The voice is standard phraseology: short fixed words (`open`, `RB`, `unable`, `human-typing`, `budget-paused`), no filler, no guessing. Nothing announces success before it is confirmed: a send stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` reads it back (for `/clear`, until its new-session post-condition does; for `/compact` on a verified CLI, until its same-session compact post-condition does, and on an unverified CLI `/compact` stays `unconfirmable`). Missing readings print `unknown`, and old information carries its age (`read 4m ago`, `expired`). It is explicitly NOT a monitoring dashboard: no status dots, toasts, graphs, spinners or glow.
**Expression:** base 0.2 · frontend N/A (viola has no web or graphical frontend) · CLI TTY 0.2 · `--json`/non-TTY/`NO_COLOR`/`TERM=dumb`/`viola run` and `viola revive` passthrough 0.0.

**Signature:** the readback box — a fixed-width 1px-ruled square cell whose one place is the CLI mirror: `open` (outline) · `RB` / `read back` (solid buff fill, graphite `RB`) · `unable` (1px `/` strike + reason) · `unconfirmable` (open drawing, never filled). CLI mirror `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]`. Supporting element: the **cocked strip** (`dialog_pending`: the row keeps its slot and shows `DIALOG <kind>`, the word amber on the CLI).
| Surface (ladder 1) | `#1E2124` | first of three surfaces (no surface scale: viola renders no page) |
| Surface (ladder 2) | `#2A2E33` | second of three surfaces (no surface scale: viola renders no page) |
| Ink (graphite) | `#3B3A36` | the third ink (no text hierarchy: viola renders no page) |
CLI colour: amber on the `DIALOG` word only, SGR dim on a whole `stale` row, bold for NAME; handoff blue is never used and backgrounds are never set.
- **No type tokens:** viola renders no page; the cli's type is the terminal's.
- **cli:** terminal monospace (the user's configured font); the brand shows through the fixed-column structure and the phraseology words.
- Bold only for the NAME column, SGR dim for `stale` rows, amber for the `DIALOG` word; ASCII only, high density. No font stacks or render assertions: viola renders no page.
- No spacing tokens (viola renders no page): CLI spacing is platform-controlled, a fixed-width terminal grid, two spaces between columns.
- **Calibrated to the base expression 0.2:** the cli (0.2 on a TTY, 0.0 otherwise) has no motion at all, and viola renders no page.
- No depth or radius tokens (viola renders no page); the cli draws no depth, and square brackets `[ ]` keep the ruled-rectangle reading.
- **web-spa** — no web surface: viola renders no page; the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14) takes its own surface section at the route entry «Console scaffold»

- **CLI** — `viola list` (the k9s-style board, six fixed columns and words the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) reuses; as built: uncoloured under `--json`, a piped stdout, `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included) or `TERM=dumb`, else NAME bold, the `DIALOG` word amber with its kind word plain and a wrapped `stale` row dim end to end; on a terminal whose width is known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME too long for its column is cut with `...`; the wrapped rows, then, when one `claude agents --json` read lists a session no wrapped row joins, the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line and one row per unwrapped session (NAME its `sessionId`, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI); STATUS `idle` / `busy` on a row the read joins, else `unknown`; a failed read prints the board as with no `claude`; and a failed strict-modes check refuses the whole board with exit 21, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`), the `viola send` readback mirror (an unusable `viola send` and an oversize `viola answer` instead exit 2 with their fixed stderr line, `UNUSABLE_TEXT` / `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE`, whatever `--json` says, and no document; a failed `cli` verb's `error: internal error`, exit 1, is with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` the document `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty, while `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent at the catch site), phraseology verb output (`viola plugin install`: four plain-ASCII stdout lines in one write, no SGR, `viola@viola  written  <dir>` / `run these to add it to Claude Code:` / `  claude plugin marketplace add <dir>` / `  claude plugin install viola@viola`, `<dir>` quoted only where the host's shell would split it; under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}`; a refused strict-modes check is exit 21 with `viola list`'s home pair on stderr, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty), `viola wait` / `viola last` (one static result line on stdout, no spinner; a `wait` woken by an expired dialog hold prints `dialog-expired  <name>  dialog <id>  cursor <n>`, ASCII, no SGR, written once), `viola link` / `viola unlink` (one plain-ASCII stdout line in one write, no SGR, exit 0: `link    <driver> -> <driven>  since <HH:MM:SSZ>`, `link    <driver> -> <driven>  already linked` for a held pair, `unlink  <driver> -> <driven>` whether or not a pair was removed; under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":<ts>,"already_linked":<bool>}}` / `{"v":1,"ok":{}}`; a refused strict-modes check of the driven instance is exit 21 with `revive`'s instance pair on stderr naming it, and so is the one `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` make of their instance before any frame (that pair, not the `[/ ]` mirror; no frame and no line written), or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty (exit 21's document is `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, `<cause>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`)), `viola verify` step counter, the `viola run` / `viola revive` passthrough (nothing printed while the child runs; `viola revive <name> --list` prints one static line per logged session; under `--json` both arms print one stdout document: `--list`'s `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}`, every refusal of the start it shares with `run`, `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with exit 1, no hint and stderr empty, `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`; a `pump_child` error prints none, the child having held the terminal)
- The readback box — the signature; its one place the `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]` column of CLI `viola send`
- Transfer markers — only `link` / `unlink` verb output (`overseer -> builder`), plain, ASCII `->`, no inbound form; `viola list` has no link column
- The tower tape — the ndjson tape in `events.ndjson`; the CLI has no tape, and terminal scrollback is the history
- The BAY line — the one static header, atop `viola list`: `BAY`, `5H`, `7D`, `read … ago`, gate, `skipped` (no TAPE cell)
- Refusal lines — `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>` on stderr, then the cause's `hint:` line last
- NEVER use a ninth hex value: all eight come from the Color World, and only two are hues.
- NEVER use glow or a terminal-green / neon "hacker" theme; the cli draws no depth.
- A refused send folds into its send line; `turn-ended` never fills a readback box; a nonzero `skipped` count stays visible; a bare strip is never cocked nor a target.

record.requirement: an agent can `boot`, `run`, `status`, `cleanup` and `logs` a product session on any of the three OSes through identical shell shims, each command printing exactly one JSON document and a typed exit code; `boot` reaches readiness or names the unmet check, `cleanup` is idempotent and proves endpoints, ports and token files are gone, and `status` shows the CLI board and the GUI sessions agree.

verification.acceptance: On each of the three CI OSes (the run the chunk's `ci.py conclusion` entry reads), the `scripts/agent-run.*` shims drive a fake-agent session through `boot`, `run`, `status`, `cleanup` and `logs`, each command printing exactly one JSON document and exiting 0, 1 or 2; `boot` reaches readiness or names its unmet check; `status` exits 0 with `state:"ready"` and a `list` member that is the `viola list --json` document naming the booted instance `wrapped:true, liveness:"live"`; `cleanup` run twice exits 0 with `processes_gone` and `endpoint_gone` true — witnessed by `ci.yml`'s harness lifecycle step on the three runners and by `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs` / `harness_lifecycle.rs` under `run --coverage`. title: Every exit-21 and exit-1 cause has a machine-readable code

record.title: Every exit-21 and exit-1 cause has a machine-readable code
record.requirement: every cause of exit 21 (not running, unwrapped name, strict-modes, server verification, endpoint lost mid-call) and of exit 1 (already live, stale heartbeat, squatted name, pinned-hash mismatch, script child, strict-modes or socket-directory refusal, internal error) reaches `--json`, MCP and the process log as a distinct code with no path or pid, matching the human hint for the same cause.
record.observed_gap: exit 21 and exit 1 each have several causes; design now gives one hint per cause in human mode, but arch fixes `{"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` for exit 21 and gives exit 1 no `--json` document (A:292-294; DS cli pattern 2 "pending an arch amendment"); obs's codes lack stale heartbeat and unwrapped name (OB §6 detail code catalog, D-20), and strict-modes or socket-directory refusals at `run`/`ui`/`mcp` start have no code (XF X7, T4, F4, B6).

verification.acceptance: Each cause reaches its own closed code on each surface it reaches, carrying no path or pid and matching the human hint of that cause. Exit 21: strict-modes-failed, instance-dead (not running), unwrapped-name, endpoint-lost and server-verify-failed, printed in detail under --json as {"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"} and returned by MCP as the same body less v, its text refused: instance-unreachable; on the process log as the process-exit detail of each cause a log is open for, exit 21 at WARN, endpoint-lost with during call. Exit 1, in the error of {"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null} on revive --json and the catch site under --json, and in the process-exit detail: strict-modes-failed, already-live, no-session, session-live, cwd-missing, stale-heartbeat, batch-script-child, pinned-hash-mismatch, squatted-name, internal-error; verify's refusals on the process-exit it writes under a VIOLA_NAME: program-not-found, version-unreadable, unclean-fixture, pinned-hash-mismatch, batch-script-child, strict-modes-failed, interrupted. Each human form ends stderr with that cause's own hint: line (internal-error none), and no hint two codes share (tests/cross_exit_causes.rs no_two_codes_share_a_hint beside its planted-duplicate control shared_hints_reads_a_planted_duplicate). Witnesses: tests/cross_exit_causes.rs, crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs, tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs, tests/cli_instance_state.rs, tests/cli_verify.rs. Named apart, on the founder's own word (chunks/2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue/inputs/I2-relay-1.md.txt Q4): a strict-modes check refused before a log opens writes no line; MCP reaches only the exit-21 causes its five tools can meet and writes no line, isError its record; run and verify have no --json, so their causes reach the log and the hint, run's start also through revive --json; viola mcp's own exit 1 keeps both streams empty; macOS's server check and the socket-directory refusal stay with the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening".

title: `send` types at a turn boundary and is confirmed after the fact

record.title: `send` types at a turn boundary and is confirmed after the fact
record.requirement: a driver's text (from stdin or a file, never a leading-slash argument, with a warning on a rewritten path) is typed as one paste plus Enter only when the input box is ready; it returns read back only when the matching prompt is seen, `not-delivered` with a typed detail otherwise (`input-not-ready`, `no-prompt-submitted`, `turn-running`, `control-character`), and `unconfirmable` only for a ledger-listed local command without a measured post-condition; `/clear` is confirmed by its new-session post-condition; text with a disallowed control character is refused, never stripped.
record.observed_gap: the prototype sends without a readiness gate; a CLI-native modal swallowed a paste (M1), local commands fire no prompt event (M5), and Git Bash rewrote a leading-slash argument (B §6).

verification.acceptance: A driver's text from stdin or a file is typed as one bracketed paste plus Enter and returns read back only when the matching prompt is observed (`path2_send_confirms_with_cl1_events`, `tests/cli_send.rs`); on a verified CLI it is typed only when the input box is ready (`send_on_a_verified_cli_refuses_while_the_trust_dialog_is_up`); otherwise it returns not-delivered with a typed detail: input not ready (the same case), no prompt submitted (`send_window_no_prompt_submitted_refuses_and_logs`), turn running (`send_window_second_concurrent_send_is_refused_turn_running`, `send_after_a_confirmed_send_is_turn_running_until_turn_ended`), control character (`setting_does_not_disable_the_send_paste_control`, `tests/cli_controls_not_disableable.rs`, and the unit table `send_refusal_order`); unconfirmable appears only for a ledger-listed local command without a measured post-condition (`send_window_local_command_is_not_presumed_delivered`: `/clear` on an unverified CLI and `/remote-control` each exit 0 with `{confirmed:false, detail:"unconfirmable", cursor}`; `send_window_slash_text_off_the_list_is_not_delivered`: a slash text off the list ends not-delivered; the unit functions `send_local_command_without_a_measured_post_condition_is_unconfirmable` and `send_local_command_decision_is_exact_text_never_a_leading_slash`); title: CLI and terminal output discipline

record.title: CLI and terminal output discipline
record.requirement: on all three OSes, CLI output is linear and static (one `waiting:` line on a TTY only, no carriage-return redraw or cursor movement), no colour or glyphs under non-TTY, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb` or `--json`, every colour span sits beside its word (amber only on `DIALOG`, dim only on stale rows), injected control characters in `wait`/`last`/`list` output appear only escaped, `verify` prints appended step lines, `ui` prints its launch line once; under `viola run` viola adds zero bytes to the terminal, human keys are delivered unblocked during a driver send, and focus, mouse and resize sequences never move the wheel.
record.observed_gap: a11y makes no conformance claim for terminal surfaces but binds output discipline for them: no spinner or redraw, colour only beside its word, controls escaped, and the wrapped TUI untouched (AY P4, P6).

verification.acceptance:
On ubuntu-latest, macos-latest and windows-2025 every human-mode CLI output keeps the terminal discipline, each clause held by its named witness:
(1) Linear and static: `wait_human_lines_are_linear` reads `waiting: <name>` exactly once on stderr under the outer PTY and none piped, and on Unix `viola wait`'s and `viola --help`'s terminal streams hold no ESC byte and no CR not followed by LF (`wait_human_lines_are_linear`, `help_is_plain_on_a_terminal`).
(2) No colour or glyphs under a non-TTY stdout, `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included), `TERM=dumb` or `--json`: `cross_list_rows_print_no_sgr_under_no_color_dumb_piped_or_json` (zero ESC on Unix, an SGR attribute set within {0} on windows-2025) and one `colour_decision_each_rung_switches_colour_off` case per rung.
(3) Every colour span beside its word: `cross_list_rows_style_each_span_beside_its_word_on_a_terminal` reads bold only around NAME values and the attention token only around the `DIALOG` word (its kind word plain), no dim on a live board, the depth by `COLORTERM` / `TERM`; the `board_row_style_*` units hold dim only on a stale row with the cocked composition (the `DIALOG` word amber and not dim), and `unable` / `fail` carry no SGR.
(4) Injected controls appear only escaped in `wait`, `last` and `list` output: the `last` case of `tests/cli_wait_last.rs`, `cross_list_rows_print_escaped_in_the_captions_columns_in_every_mode`, the `escape_*` units and `board_row_style_*` (g), which reads an escaped control the same at every depth.
(5) `viola verify` appends one `[NN/MM] … pass|fail` step line per relied row and the `stamped` summary: the `tests/cli_verify.rs` literals.
(6) Under `viola run` viola adds zero bytes to the terminal: the `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` cases (byte for byte against an unwrapped run on Unix, viola's literals absent on windows-2025).
(7) Human keys pass unblocked during a driver send: `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` (the key reaches the child, the send exits 10 `human-typing` with nothing typed) and `paste_human_bytes_during_a_paste_land_wholly_after_it`.
(8) Focus, mouse and resize never move the wheel: `tui_focus_mouse_and_resize_never_take_the_wheel` (Unix in full; windows-2025 by the founder's F-W3 platform fact).
On windows-2025 the terminal readings of (1)–(4) and (6) are read by literal absence or parsed SGR attributes, because ConPTY re-renders the stream. The dim span on a real stale row is held at the unit tier over the writer's own bytes. The `ui` launch-line clause is out of 0.1.0 by the founder's 2026-10-16 ruling.

title: The IPC endpoint admits only the same OS user and verifies its server

record.title: The IPC endpoint admits only the same OS user and verifies its server
record.requirement: on each OS only the owning user (and SYSTEM on Windows) can connect; remote pipe clients and other users' peers are rejected; every client verifies it is talking to the recorded wrapper process before writing any frame, and on mismatch CLI/MCP report unreachable while hooks fail open; a squatted name blocks start rather than being taken over; macOS's missing pid check is recorded as a known gap.
record.observed_gap: the endpoint is a code-execution interface with predictable names in shared namespaces (S:21, S:55-71).

verification.acceptance: On each OS only the owning user (and SYSTEM on Windows) can connect to an instance endpoint; remote pipe clients and other users' peers are rejected; every client verifies it is talking to the recorded wrapper process before writing any frame, and on mismatch the CLI and MCP report unreachable while hooks fail open; a squatted name blocks start rather than being taken over; the missing macOS pid check is recorded as a known gap. Witnesses. Unix admission: tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs (a socket directory at 0755 or a symlink refused at run, the eight CLI frame verbs and the hook, on Linux and macOS), crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs handlers_frame_tools_refuse_a_loosened_socket_directory, and, since a second account cannot be driven on a hosted runner (test-plan section 1), the wrapper's and the clients' decision over an injected foreign euid (crates/viola-channel/src/client.rs, the peer_euid_admitted table) and accept_loop's refusing unit in crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs, a refused stream reaching no dispatch, beside channel_endpoint_answers_protocol_faults serving a same-user peer. Windows: tests/security_negatives_channel.rs (remote rejection, the DACL's effect). Client verification: tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs on Linux and Windows, the impostor rows of tests/hook_fail_open.rs, crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs handlers_frame_tools_write_no_frame_to_a_server_that_is_not_the_recorded_wrapper; the euid read at every Unix client, macOS included, client_server_euid_is_this_user and its Tokio twin. A squatted name: tests/path1_run_start.rs and tests/cross_exit_causes.rs a_held_endpoint_is_squatted_name. The macOS gap: server_verdict_rows' no-comparison row (crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs), the server-identity negatives compiled out on macOS, and the named carve-out in the masters, no test reading that match as a comparison.

title: .claude/docs/gotchas.md

body:
**What breaks:** designing against docs misses real flags (`stream-json` input, `claude attach`) and real behaviours.
**How to avoid:** design against the installed CLI, measured; every relied-on behaviour is a ledger row with a `viola verify` probe (StopFailure excepted: registered with no ledger row and no verify probe).
**References:** brief §4; arch [CLI Version Compatibility].

title: .claude/docs/services/viola-agent-claude.md

body: - `hook` module (as landed): `HookEvent` (10 registered events, `StopFailure` among them, the dialog tier `PreToolUse` / `PermissionRequest` included; `from_arg`, `kind()` — an `Option<EventKind>`, `None` for the dialog tier — `is_dialog()`, `as_str` = diag-line `$defs.hook_event`), `normalise(event, bytes) -> Normalised{kind, data, drift}` (StopFailure (`viola hook stop-failure`) maps to `turn-ended`, not a dialog, its data exactly `last_assistant_message` null, `background_tasks` null and `cause` `api-error`; Stop's `turn-ended` data is `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks}`, with no `cause`: `background_tasks` the payload array's length only, no element read or carried, `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array). A wrong-typed known field → a drift entry `{path, expected:"string"}` and read as absent. Prompt order: classify `harness` on the RAW prefix, no trim (`HARNESS_PREFIXES`: `<agent-message from=` / `<task-notification>` / `<\cross-session-message` / `<cross-session-message` — the escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies; as measured on 2.1.287 a real cross-session message arrived unescaped under `from` / `from-name` / `from-mode`, and a `<task-notification>` typed at a prompt's very start arrives as typed and is filed `harness`), then unwrap only the CLI's unescaped same-id pair `<pasted_content id="X">\n…\n</pasted_content id="X">` together with the frame the CLI writes around it (the two newlines directly before the open tag, the one directly after the close tag, and a second after it when text follows that is not the next pair's own two-newline frame; a third before, a second after at the prompt's end and a lone one before stay, an unmatched open tag removes nothing; one id serves every pair of a session), then un-escape `<\` before an ASCII letter or `/` — a typed pair is never unwrapped. A pasted text's last newline never reaches the hook (measured on 2.1.287, wrapped or not), so `text` lacks it. No `send` relies on this: `typed_text(text)` returns a sent text with every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters, every one of them in any order (a `Cow<'_, str>`, borrowed unless an inner CR is replaced; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes: not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and the root bin's `send` types and classifies that typed text and matches a `prompt-submitted` text equal to it, or non-empty and equal to it less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF, the text kept as submitted; the client's `refusal_of` is its second product caller (the founder's rulings, 2026-10-07T15:21Z for a trailing LF, 2026-10-09 for a trailing CR and CRLF, 2026-10-09T16:51Z for a CR or a CR LF inside; architecture [Delivery Confirmation]). An LF typed inside a paste is submitted unchanged (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text); every multi-line `send` relies on it, and it is gated by the ledger row `paste-newline` and its `viola verify` probe, Run B's `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (landed at chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, stamped on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host). The frame beside typed text and between two pairs is unit-held and unprobed (`viola verify` types only lone pastes), and no probe is owed: a shape no `send` relies on needs none (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-07). StopFailure is registered with no ledger row and no verify probe.

title: CLAUDE.md

body:
<!-- GENERATED:setup:architecture start -->
viola is mechanism, not policy: it carries typed input, answers dialogs when told to, logs everything and holds the wheel, but never decides what to answer — driver-side policy (Andromeda's decision rights included) stays outside the binary. Every behaviour of the `claude` CLI it relies on is a measured, version-stamped capability-ledger row (StopFailure alone is registered with no ledger row and no verify probe); on an unverified CLI build viola degrades to transport-only and every send is confirmed after the fact (`prompt-submitted` read-back or a ledger post-condition), never presumed, the one exception a ledger-listed local command whose post-condition is none or not yet measured, or whose CLI is unverified: `ok` with `confirmed: false`, detail `unconfirmable`.

title: .claude/docs/design-summary.md

body: **"Strip-bay handoff, read back."** The direction the CLI carries, and the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) inherits, is an air-traffic-control tower strip bay after dark. Buff paper strips sit in anthracite holder boots on ruled aluminium racks, and every session keeps its slot for life. The only warm light is the one amber arrival holder cocked out of line when a session needs you. The voice is standard phraseology: short fixed words (`open`, `RB`, `unable`, `human-typing`, `not-delivered`), no filler, no guessing. Nothing announces success before it is confirmed: a send stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` reads it back (its prompt equal to the sent text or to it with a trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR or LF removed; any leading or inner difference leaves it unconfirmed) (on a verified CLI, for `/clear` until its new-session post-condition does and for `/compact` until its same-session compact post-condition does; on an unverified CLI both `/clear` and `/compact` stay `unconfirmable`). Missing readings print `unknown`. It is explicitly NOT a monitoring dashboard: no status dots, toasts, graphs, spinners or glow.

title: .claude/docs/security-summary.md

body: - `validate_paste_text` allows LF/CR/TAB (multi-line relays are normal), rejects the rest — reject, never strip a refused character. Only allowed characters are rewritten or removed: after validation `send` types the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, and the delivery confirmation, the local-command list, `text_bytes` and the paste read that typed text (delivery is confirmed when the submitted text equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals it with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; no other difference, leading trimming included, is tolerated), which holds no CR (the founder's rulings, 2026-10-07T15:21Z for a trailing LF, 2026-10-09 for a trailing CR and CRLF, 2026-10-09T16:51Z for a CR or a CR LF inside). An empty typed text is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13), by the client before any frame and by the wrapper before the first wheel read.

- Test homes on the Linux dev host (the founder's live answer, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer; a boundary widening): `target/e2e-home` is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so the fixture chain's sweep and drop and harness `cleanup` create and delete outside the working directory, each only a dir the test side itself made (by its owner record, its own temp dir or its session name prefix) or another build's stamp dir whose lock it takes with try_lock. The two keepers follow a linked base only when its target is absolute and one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refuse a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), each refusal a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts); they create it 0700 and remove nothing. `viola` never names the backing; no CI runner has the link. Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`): the round runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog; the rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key (on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, any other screen no key; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send); the CLI's writes are its own — its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings); viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`. Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI): one `viola run` start of the CLI under a tmpfs `--home`, in a detached 80×24 pane, its cwd a fresh `.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root, with no key typed; one `viola list` read against that home; at two instants the pane's bottom three screen rows, scrubbed of the home and the user word, written to the chunk's `evidence/`, never a row above the footer; then the start is killed and its cwd removed; it left no transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` (as measured on 2.1.302 at chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows). It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer. A live session's screen frames are kept only under a gitignored local path, never in a work dir, a run dir or a commit; what lands is a closed-word summary per frame.

title: .claude/rules/security.md

body: - A non-`null` dialog decision requires a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version (exception: StopFailure is registered with no capability ledger row and no verify probe, owned by the 2.1.325 recorded fixture set); `release` carrying a string `from` → `-32602 release-from-driver` (a `from` of another type → `-32602` with `data: null`); `from` is self-reported, never identity.

- `validate_paste_text` over decoded `char`s: allow LF/CR/TAB, refuse every other C0, DEL and C1 with `not-delivered` / `control-character` — reject, never strip a refused character. After validation the wrapper's `send` types the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`; it holds no CR, only CR and LF are rewritten or removed, and no refused character is typed or removed), and the delivery confirmation, the local-command list, `text_bytes` and the paste read that typed text (delivery is confirmed when the submitted text equals the typed text exactly, or is non-empty and equals it with its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF removed; no other difference, leading trimming included, is tolerated). An empty typed text, the empty text included, is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13) right after `control-character`: by the client before any frame and by the wrapper before the first wheel read.

title: .claude/rules/testing.md

body: - Fixtures `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json` (the CLI's PascalCase hook event name, e.g. `PreToolUse.ask.json`; no mapping table; StopFailure is registered with no recorded payload, ledger row or verify probe, and its tests use a synthetic StopFailure payload), and the recorded MCP exchanges `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/Mcp.<variant>.json` (e.g. `Mcp.tools-list-1.json`, recorded by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap`, schema `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json`); fake scripts `fixtures/fake-scripts/<scenario>.json` (schema `schemas/fake-script.v1.json`).

title: .claude/docs/a11y-summary.md

body: - **P3 — dialog pending, then `answer`** — cli (`viola answer` for a question, permission, plan, or a question first raised by PermissionRequest; `unverified-cli` refusal)

- Every time bound viola holds (wait timeout and cap, MCP call deadline, dialog hold, send readiness gate, paste write, confirmation windows, agents read, the start's Claude config lock wait) falls on the driver, viola's child or viola's own start; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. An MCP frame tool call (send, wait, last, answer) that outlives the MCP call deadline (`viola_mcp::MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`) ends `instance-unreachable` / `call-deadline`, the outcome of a send unknown; only the MCP frame tools write that detail, never the CLI, whose exit-21 cause set stays six. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list` and `viola revive` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP`, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` at `WAIT_CAP`: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched.
