title: .claude/docs/services/viola.md

body: The `viola` binary. It holds the clap 4.6.7 dispatch (`src/main.rs`, one module per subcommand in `src/cmd/`) and the `run` wrapper (`src/run/`): the PTY pump, the wheel, the readiness-gate wiring and the channel server dispatch. It also owns the pinned copy + plugin write-out, the obs init (`viola::obs`: `MillisUtc`, `viola_obs_init`, the panic hook, the detail writer, the catch-site reporter `report_internal_error`; `open_role_file` and `write_detail` run `strict::check_diagnostics` on an existing `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything — a symbolic link refused, a folder to the read rule, a file to the read rule, an absent path passing — and a refusal is a failed open: the writer ends at `std::io::sink`, a detail line is dropped) and the human/`--json` output modules (the `human` module: `src/human.rs`, with its phases under `src/human/` — mirror, escape, board, style (the colour layer: `Depth`, `Tokens`, `Facts`, `decide`, `read`), wait, verbs, hints —; `src/human.rs` holds the stderr refusal writer `write_refusal` behind `refuse`, the stderr `write_internal_error` (`error: internal error\n`) behind `internal_error`, and the stdout `write_result` behind `result`, each one `write_all`; called by `run`, `revive`, `verify`, `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `plugin install` and the `main` catch site; no print macro, no `#[allow]`). `viola verify` (`src/cmd/verify.rs`) drives the one print-mode probe and then the six interactive PTY runs, with one print-mode sender, `verify-sender`, inside Run B's cross-session turn (Run B addressed by its inbox socket `uds:<runtime>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`, from the runtime dir and its pid, never by a bare session id) (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` and its children under `src/cmd/verify/typed/`: Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with compiled pastes — the probe prompt, then the long text, the tag-like text, the newline text (`PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE`, 113 bytes, one inner LF), `/compact` (`PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND`), `/clear` and `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent` (the `local-command-echo` row's probe, passing on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window; with no readable transcript the paste skipped and the row failing), then eighth `/context` (the relied `local-command-context` row's probe, passing on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window; a failing read of it is `fail`, never `absent`), each added one only into a settled input box, waited for after an added text turn and after the `/compact` turn up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (`box_wait`: 2.1.287 shows a paste hint in the input-box literal's place for 8.0 s after a long paste) — and, once its first turn has settled and before its framing pastes, ONE `claude agents --json` read (`typed::turns::agents_read`: Run B's program, cwd the probe dir, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read; its capture kept in memory, never written to the captures dir; no live start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/` (among them a compiled prompt raising a question through PermissionRequest, answered by the closed probe id `permission-question-first-option`: the relied `permission-request-question` row passing only when that request is raised and the answer reaches the tool's answers), Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E trusted in `-resume/`, resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (`viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)`, the id Run B's first SessionStart `session_id` through `ledger::resume_target`; empty input, no `--settings`, ended by a kill), then last Run F, after Run E, starting in an untrusted folder for which verify wrote a trust record (the `trust-record` row passing only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal, and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; verify writes that record for its own temp folder only into the Claude config file its child reads, located through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `claude_env_keep` keeps it, never creating an absent file, and removes that one record after; `run`'s and `revive`'s start, on a verified CLI, write the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder); no key into any dialog — the hidden `hook --capture --answers` arm in `src/cmd/hook.rs` answers C and D's from `PROBE_ANSWERS`), checks the relied ledger rows (`check_rows` walks `LedgerRow::relied()`: every row of `LedgerRow::ALL` on every build, the relied `local-command-echo` among them; the relied cross-session-prefix row passing only when the print-mode sender's message to Run B, started with the crossSessionInbound accept settings, arrives opening with the CLI's cross-session harness prefix, else failing, never on the sender's words, and with no runtime dir running no turn; the relied identity-floor row passing when every CLAUDE name the CLI adds to a SessionStart hook, kept names dropped first, is an identity-floor or known non-identity name, and failing on an unknown name or an unread or off-shape env-names file), prints the step lines (each `pass`, `absent` or `fail`) and `stamped` summary (its pass count including an absent `browser-tools-prompt`, the one relied row whose `absent` counts toward verified) and writes the stamps through `viola_state::stamps::update_stamps` (its `StampsError::StrictModes` refusal printing the home-state pair, exit 1); before its `cli` log opens it runs `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, None, None)` (the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`, each that exists), a refusal printing the home pair and exiting 1 with no step line, no summary and no line; a verify stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`cmd::verify::stop`: `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, installed by `viola verify` alone, its handler only setting one process-global flag that every wait of the run reads) kills and reaps the running child with no key, starts no later run, writes no stamp and exits 1 (`unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, stdout empty), its drop guards removing only the dirs, and its own trust record from the Claude config file, that run created; SIGKILL, a crash and a failed handler install keep the OS default and leave the dirs to be removed by hand; `run::version_gate` reads them at `run` start. The panic detail backtrace is raw, never-symbolised frames (`src/panic_frames.rs`). It is the only crate with anyhow (dispatch edge and the catch-site reporter) and tracing-subscriber, and it consumes only normalised events.

- `run` start order (before the wrapper log opens, every start, `run`'s and a revived one, checks the home tree: `checked_exe` reads the exe's bytes once and takes their pin key, then `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree` checks the home, the instance's set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists — a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair, or the instance pair for an instance-level refusal, no log opened, no line and no child —, and the pin step pins those same bytes through `pin_bytes`; the home is canonicalised by `canonical_home` once the wrapper log has created it, before the collision check, the pin and the endpoint bind): program resolution (a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`; it writes nothing) → collision check → pinned copy (placed once when absent, with no clobber, through `place_private_new`, and never replaced; SHA-256 re-hash on reuse and of a copy a concurrent first start placed first; a mismatch → exit 1 `pinned-hash-mismatch`, the file left as found) + plugin folder rewrite → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: `--version` with no user args, killed at 5 s, logged as a `version-probe` start/exit pair; the stamps read; `cli_version` / `cli_verified` (the start's final verdict: the gate's, its stamps read again after an automatic verify where one ran) into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; nothing printed) → `socket_dir_ready` (`src/cmd/run.rs`: `check_endpoint_dir`, create the parent only when absent, check again; a refused or uncreatable directory → exit 1 `socket-dir-refused`, left as found, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, the `unable:` / `hint:` pair and one `process-exit`; a `Server::bind` failure does not read this code) → exclusive endpoint bind (taken → exit 1 `squatted-name`) → any automatic verify (with `config.json`'s `verify_new_cli` on, default off, and no attempted stamps entry for the claude version: `viola verify` run once as a child, the home passed to it only through `--home`, only while holding the owner-only `ledger/verify.lock`, try-locked after the stamps strict-modes check and never the stamps lock, a held lock meaning no verify and an unverified start; an entry already attempted, a red one included, never verified again automatically; the start gating on the final verdict) → on a verified verdict, the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder written into the child's Claude config (located through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `claude_env_keep` keeps it) → first snapshot (with `endpoint`) + heartbeat → `wheel` event → child spawn (R8 strip, `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN`, pinned folder first on PATH, `--plugin-dir`) → snapshot rewritten with `child_pid`. A live holder or a fresh replayed beat → exit 1 `already-live`, a `stale` holder → exit 1 `stale-heartbeat` (the `run.collision_check` span's `outcome` reads `already-live` for both); a `gone` one is taken over at once. The collision check takes its caller's one snapshot read (`replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`): over a replayed snapshot, which holds no `pid` or `started_at`, it decides from the heartbeat alone, a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old refusing `already-live` and an older one free; a failed read or no snapshot is free. The first snapshot records the spawn directory as `cwd` when it is valid UTF-8.

title: .claude/rules/events.md

body: - SessionStart → `session-start` (`cause` startup|clear|resume|compact|unknown, `agent_session_id`; the hook may send an optional string `transcript` param beside `event`, never inside it, only when the transcript path passes the shape check against its own session id; the wrapper re-validates it for a session-start line only, drops any other, and it never enters event data); UserPromptSubmit → `prompt-submitted` (`text` normalised: long-paste wrapper removed, then tag escaping reversed; `origin` driver|human|harness — the hook files only human|harness; the wrapper relabels a CLI-fired scheduled wake `harness`, and `driver` comes only from the wrapper's relabel of the in-flight send's own prompt, matched on the send's typed text, the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, or on a non-empty text equal to that typed text less its trailing run of ASCII space, TAB, CR and LF, the text kept as submitted); PreToolUse AskUserQuestion → `question`; PreToolUse ExitPlanMode → `plan`; PermissionRequest → `permission`, or `question` for an AskUserQuestion call with no matching armed dialog (a PermissionRequest repeating the armed `question` / `plan` dialog's tool with an equal `tool_input` is that dialog's continuation and raises no event; a question first raised by PermissionRequest with no matching armed dialog is held for the driver and its answer returns as PermissionRequest allow with `updatedInput`, the tool input plus answers and annotations, while a human key, an expired hold or an unverified CLI leave it to the human); Stop → `turn-ended` (`last_assistant_message` or `null`; `background_tasks`, the Stop payload's `background_tasks` array length, a count only, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array; `scheduled_wakes`, the Stop payload's `session_crons` array length, a count only, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array); StopFailure (`viola hook stop-failure`) → `turn-ended`, not a dialog (data exactly `last_assistant_message` null, `background_tasks` null, `scheduled_wakes` null and `cause` one of the nine `TurnEndCause` words, classified from the CLI's error word inside the Claude adapter); SessionEnd → `session-end`; Notification / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure → `activity`.

title: .claude/docs/commands.md

body: - `viola verify [--record <dir>] [-- <program> [args…]]` — drive one print-mode probe (Haiku) and six interactive PTY runs (Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with compiled pastes (the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like text, a text holding one inner LF, `/compact`, `/clear`, then `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, the local-command-echo row's probe, skipped with that row failed when no transcript is readable, then `/context`, the local-command-context row's probe, a failing read of it `fail`, never `absent`) and one `claude agents --json` read once its first turn has settled, before the added pastes (held in memory, spawn pair `agents-probe`, no start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it) and one print-mode sender, `verify-sender`, inside Run B's cross-session turn (Run B started with the crossSessionInbound accept settings, the sender addressing it by `uds:<runtime>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`, never a bare session id; the cross-session-prefix row passes only when the message arrives opening with the CLI's cross-session harness prefix, else fails; no runtime dir runs no turn), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/` (among them a compiled prompt raising a question through PermissionRequest, answered by the closed probe id `permission-question-first-option`: the permission-request-question row passes only when that request is raised and the answer reaches the tool's answers), Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E in `-resume/` resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (input empty, no `--settings`), then Run F in an untrusted temp folder whose trust record verify writes into the Claude config file its child reads (never creating an absent file; a run or revive start writes a record only for its own untrusted spawn folder, on a verified CLI), passing the trust-record row only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; no key into any dialog — the probe hook answers C and D's) against the CLI (default `claude`), check the relied ledger rows (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build), print `[NN/MM]` step lines ending `pass`, `absent` or `fail` (`absent` on the browser-tools-prompt row alone, when no run met the CLI's browser-tools prompt; `MM` the relied count; the last `[MM/MM] browser-tools-prompt …`) + the `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` summary on stdout (`<n>` counting every relied row that counts toward verified, an absent browser-tools-prompt among them) and write `ledger/stamps.json`; exit 1 on a failing row; exit 1 with the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, no step line, no summary and no log line when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens (and the same pair, exit 1, after the step lines, when `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`, with `detail:"strict-modes-failed"` on its `process-exit` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`); a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM kills its child with no key, removes only the probe dirs it created and its own trust record from the Claude config file, writes no stamp, leaves stdout empty, prints `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` and exits 1 (SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leaves the dirs to remove by hand). `--record <dir>` also writes the scrubbed `<dir>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants, Run B's `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants, Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json`, Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only), the env-names fixture `Env.recorded-1.json` (names only, never a value: `v` 1 plus `added`) and signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens (a footer or modal row whole, the input box's rule row as its rule chars alone and its prompt row as the prompt char alone, every other row empty; a box whose live prompt row holds a home path, the username or an email refuses the recording) when 0 rows fail; an unclean recording is refused naming the file and check code. A hidden `--record-first-screens`, absent from `--help` and passed only by the live rig, makes a failed `--record` verify write a first-screen file of whole scrubbed rows per run short of the input box (Run A's trust excepted), refused whole when unclean, kept locally and never committed. Run it from a folder you trust in Claude Code whose external CLAUDE.md import is answered. Against the real CLI: local only, spends tokens; CI runs it only against the fake agent's `-p/--print` mode and its `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root --dialogs --framing --transcript --trust-config` interactive modes, under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only and named to the fake agent by `--trust-config`, with a short owner-only runtime dir (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) the test owns for the stamp's life (every stamping verify passes `--transcript` beside `--framing`, or Run B's echo probe is skipped and the local-command-echo row fails). The `Mcp.<variant>.json` MCP exchanges are recorded not by `--record` but by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (`record` / `fixture`, the same scrub and closed refusal codes; architecture §Occupied Resources → Binary); the recorded Hyprland replies likewise by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub

title: CLAUDE.md

body: - stdout is reserved per role (the hook decision body, MCP frames, `run`'s child screen, before it only a keyed start's automatic-verify lines and the verify child's own output, the CLI's `--json`): no `print!`/`println!`/`eprint!`/`eprintln!`/`dbg!` in the `hook`, `run` or `mcp` paths; events only through `obs_event!` under `#[instrument(skip_all, fields(..))]`.

title: .claude/rules/security.md

body: - Dialog hold (the budget gate and `config.json`'s `five_hour` / `seven_day` are removed, chunk 2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed): `dialog_hold_s` is read once at the wrapper's start (through `take(MAX_FRAME)`) as a whole number of seconds into `DialogHold` (60–3600, default 60); a bad value takes 60 with one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json"}` line, no value makes the hold zero or unbounded or lifts the unverified CLI gate, and no env var or flag sets it (a boundary widening the founder answered himself, chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver). No `budget.json` is read or written, and no `send` is refused for usage. A `release` with a string `from` is refused first (`release-from-driver`); after the `from` checks any `budget` key, of any value, is `-32602` invalid-params with `data: null`, no wheel moved and no record written.

title: .claude/docs/tests-summary.md

body: - **Fake agent:** `viola-fake-agent` (root `[[bin]]`, feature `fake-agent`) replays `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json` (the spine, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants and the `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants and the `SessionStart.resume-1.json` resume variant recorded by `viola verify`, the dialog tier by its Runs C and D, the framing tier by Run B's added pastes, the resume variant by Run E; `2.1.287`'s relayed dialog fixtures superseded and kept, `RELAYED.md`), runs absolute exec-form hooks from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (every SessionStart hook child given each name of its set's recorded env names, always with the fixed value `fake-agent`) (and, under `--settings-hooks <file>`, a Claude settings file's hooks beside the plugin's, a command string with no args split on spaces and never run through a shell) (a group's `matcher` evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name`), gates script steps on `--control`, and writes an ndjson `--receipt` (its modes and options taken from argv and from a fake-args file beside its exe, one argument per line within `MAX_FRAME`, put ahead of argv so argv's own value wins, never from the environment); its cross-session sender resolves its target by the uds socket address alone, delivers only to its sibling and refuses an address not of the uds shape (its PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks synthetic payloads naming the send tool), and its receiver reads its inbox only under the accept settings; its argv-only `--transcript` creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten), and every stamping `viola verify` against it (harness `boot` and the stamped-home helpers) passes it `--transcript` beside `--framing` (the framing-free verify helper passes none), and every test-started `viola verify`, `viola run` and `viola revive` and every harness boot stamping runs under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, never the runner's real `HOME` (the harness's supervised wrappers of a stamped session too, under a session user home seeded with an empty config), the fake agent told that config file by `--trust-config`, and every stamping `viola verify` of a test or the harness given a short owner-only runtime dir (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) it owns for the stamp's life (the rig rehearsal sets its own only where the host sets none) (a `--record` verify keeps the real `HOME` and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead); its print mode `-p/--print <prompt>` fires the spine fixtures, prints `ok` and exits 0, `--trust-config <file>` reads trust from that config file by the CLI's walk (the canonical cwd's exact key then each parent up to the git root, so inside a repository the cwd's own record counts, through a bounded read; any failure reads untrusted), `--screens` / `--trusted-root` / `--turn-stop` write `Screen.modal|ready|turn` (under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd it draws claude 2.1.325's unnumbered trust form over the set's recorded modal, the selector first on No; arrows move the selector, Enter on No exits 1, and SessionStart fires only after Enter on the trust row, which draws the ready screen), the argv-only `--stop-reading` makes it never read stdin, parked forever with its terminal left raw, so a paste into it blocks, `--turn-fail <variant>`, beside `--turn-stop`, ends the turn with the recorded set's `StopFailure.<variant>` payload in place of `Stop.default`, `--dialogs` replays a pasted dialog prompt's recorded variants in claim order, and `--framing` replays Run B's recorded paste, `/compact` and `/clear` variants (the probed `/compact` its recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id`; the exact verify echo probe command or the exact `/context` probe command, like a stdout-tag local command under `--local-command-mode`, one stdout tag line appended to the last started session's transcript and no hook fired) for verify's six interactive runs (two capped test-only holds: `--stop-receipt-hold-ms`, 1 s, holds the Stop receipt for a race test; `--paste-hint-ms`, 10 s, holds a cleared screen after the long paste's turn; the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` makes a start trusted by the trust record alone draw no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case; and the test-only screen switches `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` and `--long-turn-screen <phase>` draw the named screen after the tag-like paste's turn alone and after the long paste's turn alone; under `--screens` a trusted start given `--start-screen <phase>` draws `Screen.<phase>` in place of its ready screen and keeps it standing, each stdin byte one key receipt line, Ctrl-C ending it with no key line, and no byte reaching the input box) (what `viola verify` drives: `tests/cli_verify.rs` pins verify's lines by literal asserts); CI stamps homes only by running `viola verify` against it at the recorded `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`) (the root `stamped_home`, each stamped test home a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp taken per pair of built binaries, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes and taken under an exclusive lock, and harness `boot` step 4, unless `--unstamped`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified-path tests; `SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, the in-test form of `boot --unstamped` for a harness session); the real `claude` never runs in CI — only the local `run --local-live`, refused under `CI` (`live-in-ci`), and the live starts of the one standing test-only rig `viola-live-rig` in viola-e2e, run by hand under the founder's start cap for each chunk, each ledgered with its clock time first, its live arm refused under CI and its rehearsals over the fake agent run in CI (the SF arm's rehearsals unwrapped; its contained rehearsal a local entry that skips by its printed sandbox probe where the sandbox or the runtime dir cannot serve it) — and neither does the real `hyprctl`, which the same fake agent stands in for as `hyprctl` by its own file name in a test-scoped bin dir, reading its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, except in viola-hyprland's own unit tests, which serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants. The committed `fixtures/claude/*/*.json` (the recorded sets, each with its dialog, framing and resume variants and its agents fixture `Agents.recorded-1.json`, Run B's own row of its one `claude agents --json` read, where it holds them, and 2.1.287's superseded relayed fixtures included; the stamped sets are the `STAMPED` literal of `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`, each stamped at every relied row on every build, the drift-only sets its `DRIFT_ONLY`) are walked for hygiene by a run-time directory walk against `schemas/claude-fixture.v1.json`, the `Agents.*.json` agents fixtures against `schemas/claude-agents-fixture.v1.json` (`agents_fixtures_pass_hygiene`), the env-names fixture `Env.recorded-1.json` (names only, never a value, in the shape `v` 1 plus `added`, recorded by `viola verify` through the record scrub) by its own hygiene class, the `Mcp.*.json` MCP exchanges (recorded by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap`) left out of that walk and walked by `mcp_fixtures` against `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json` (`mcp_fixtures_pass_hygiene`), then replayed against `viola mcp` by `mcp_recorded_exchange` (the served `tools/list` result holding the recorded key and type shape and tool names in order), the `Screen.*.json` screens apart against `schemas/claude-screen.v1.json` (email and row-seam usernames refused too, and a box prompt row with text after the prompt char or a box rule row with any other text: a box row is recorded as its literal alone, `planted_box_row_beyond_its_literal_is_rejected`) (rstest 0.27 `#[files]` refuses an empty glob at compile time); the same walk drives the drift contract `contract_fake_agent_drift`, which compares each print-mode hook's receipt `stdin_hex` byte for byte with the recorded fixture and the hook order with the spine literal, and replays every dialog variant (a hook whose payload names the send tool left out of the dialog tier, so a side sender's hooks shift no position) and every framing variant byte for byte, and replays the resume variant (`fake_agent_resume_replay_matches_every_recorded_resume_set`) and, once resumed into its own session, the compact variant (`fake_agent_compact_replay_matches_every_recorded_compact_set`), and compares the key and type shape of the fake agent's `agents` rows with each recorded `Agents.*.json` set (`fake_agent_agents_replay_matches_every_recorded_agents_set`) (the resume launch: under `--resume <id>`, one of its argv options (`--settings <file>` accepted, its cross-session inbox read only when the value holds the accept settings and the value otherwise ignored; beside the options the mode word `agents`, a first word `agents` answering `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json` and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`, with no option and no env added), the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it (recorded by Run E since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows), else its recorded default (a set without the variant), with `source` `resume` and that `session_id`, or with `--fork-session` the compiled fork id; the `--resume` shape is the `resume-session` ledger row) ; the committed Hyprland fixtures (recorded only by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub) are walked for hygiene and against their schema too, each Hyprland reply held to its closed per-request string keep-list — no insta snapshot

- **Path 1 — `run` start sequence** — event order `wheel{start}` → `session-start` (the last start record, with a `wheel{holder:"human", cause:"human-input"}` record before it where folder-trust keys pass through the wrapper, a later human key adding none, with "Hooks to normalised events"); the home-tree strict-modes check runs before the wrapper log opens; between its exclusive endpoint bind and its first snapshot a start runs any automatic verify and then, on a verified final verdict, writes an untrusted spawn folder's trust record; duplicate / squatted / tampered-exe starts, a refused socket directory (Unix, checked before the bind) and a refused home tree exit 1; plugin files rewritten with absolute pinned paths

- **Path 2 — confirmed `send` + CL-1 records** — `cursor` = pre-paste offset, `send-issued` then `prompt-submitted{driver}` holding the submitted text (the typed text, or the typed text less the trailing run of space, TAB, CR and LF the CLI trimmed); `no-prompt-submitted` → exit 13 + `send-refused`; a second send in flight, or any send during a running turn (after a `prompt-submitted` of any origin, before `turn-ended`) → exit 13 `turn-running` (the test ends its first turn with a scripted Stop, `path3.json`, before its second send; `send_after_a_confirmed_send_is_turn_running_until_turn_ended` covers the driver's own turn); a ledger-listed local command with no measured post-condition (`/remote-control` on any version, or any listed command, `/compact`, `/clear`, `/mcp` and `/context` among them, on an unverified CLI), or an echo-confirmed command with no remembered transcript or no readable transcript end → exit 0 `unconfirmable`, `send-issued` then `send-confirmed{confirmed:false}`, no window (`send_window_local_command_is_not_presumed_delivered`; `/compact` on an unverified CLI `send_compact_on_an_unverified_cli_is_unconfirmable_at_once`); `/compact` on a verified CLI is confirmed by a `session-start` with cause `compact` and the session's own unchanged id inside its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL), else `not-delivered`/`no-prompt-submitted` at it (`send_compact_on_a_verified_cli_is_confirmed_by_its_same_session`, on the recorded 2.1.287 `compact-1` variant); `/clear` on a verified CLI is confirmed by a `session-start` with cause `clear` and a new session id (`send_clear_on_a_verified_cli_is_confirmed_by_its_new_session`, on the recorded 2.1.287 variants); `/mcp` and `/context` on a verified CLI are confirmed only by a new stdout tag in the transcript past its pre-paste end, else `not-delivered`; a slash text off the list → exit 13 `no-prompt-submitted`; a send into a child that stops reading exits 13 `not-delivered`/`paste-cut` within `PASTE_BOUND`, with the send's cursor and no Enter typed, and the next send is refused `paste-cut` with nothing issued; a text ending in newlines is typed without them and confirmed exit 0 with no `wheel` record (`send_text_ending_in_newlines_is_typed_without_them_and_confirmed`, one LF and two; `/clear` and a newline as `/clear` is unit-tier in the suites); as measured on live 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (a local live measurement, no suite): a send ending in newlines and `/clear` with a newline are confirmed; since chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup a text ending in CR, CRLF or two CRs is typed without the ending and confirmed too (the tails of the same case; live `after-cr`, `after-crlf`, `after-cr-cr`), and a text whose typed text is empty is refused at once exit 13 `not-delivered`/`empty-text` and never issued (`send_empty_text_is_refused_at_once`, `send_empty_text_straight_to_the_wrapper_is_refused`; live `after-empty-text`); since chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text a CR or a CR LF inside a text is typed as one LF and the send is confirmed with no `wheel` record (`send_text_whose_inner_cr_is_one_lf_is_typed_with_lf_and_confirmed`, three cases; live on 2.1.287 `rule-inner-crlf`, `rule-inner-cr`, `rule-inner-cr-cr`, `rule-inner-lf-cr`, `rule-crlf-lines`, after the control `rule-inner-lf` that an LF typed inside a paste is submitted unchanged, a shape covered since chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row by the ledger row `paste-newline` and its `viola verify` probe, Run B's `paste-3` paste, stamped on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host; before the rule such a send was filed `human` and ended exit 13, live `after-inner-crlf`, `after-inner-cr`); under the fake agent's paste-hint hold a send on a verified CLI waits in the gate and is delivered once the hold ends, as it is without the hold (`send_under_the_paste_hint_on_a_verified_cli`), and a key written during that wait takes the wheel and the send exits 10 `human-typing` with nothing typed (`send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins`; it cannot tell `send`'s first wheel read from its second); a long text the CLI wraps is confirmed (`send_long_text_wrapped_by_the_cli_is_confirmed`); the readiness gate, tested through its refusal outputs, has one delivered case: a send on a verified CLI past a modal label quoted in the transcript over an idle input box; a send during a blocked paste is refused `turn-running` after waiting at most the paste bound, and a hook record during the blocked paste lands within the bound; the MCP `send` step landed at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` `mcp_tools_path2_path3_send_wait_last_match_the_cli`, its result compared with the CLI's `--json` document less `v`)

title: .claude/rules/verification-harness.md

body: - Answers `--version` like the real CLI. Standing as `hyprctl` by its own file name (in a test-scoped bin dir, in place of the real `hyprctl`; viola-hyprland's own unit tests serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub instead, because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants), it reads its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, never from the env; otherwise its modes and options come from argv and from a `fake-args` file beside its exe (one argument per line within `MAX_FRAME`, put ahead of argv so argv's own value wins), never from the env. It reads hook commands from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (the `--plugin-dir` `run` passes), and under `--settings-hooks <file>` from that Claude settings file too, its hooks run beside the plugin's (a command string with no args split on spaces, never run through a shell). Only an absolute exec-form `command` is spawned: no shell, no PATH; a group's `matcher` is evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name` (`hook_commands(…, tool)`). A non-absolute command is receipted `command_absolute:false, ran:false` and never run. Every SessionStart hook child is given each name of its set's recorded env names (`Env.recorded-1.json`), always with the fixed value `fake-agent`. The payload is `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json`, with only `prompt` set for UserPromptSubmit and the fixture's trailing newline kept, so the recorded prompt yields the recorded bytes; under `--resume <id>` the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it, else its recorded `SessionStart.default` (a set without the variant), with `source` `resume` and `session_id` the id given (with `--fork-session`, the compiled fork id), and no other payload is built save the compact replay's `SessionStart.compact-1` under `--framing`, whose `session_id` is set to the last SessionStart the agent fired, under `--transcript` the launch SessionStart's `transcript_path`, and under `--stop-crons` each Stop's `session_crons`; the cross-session sender's PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks carry synthetic payloads naming the send tool, never recorded bytes.

title: .claude/rules/observability.md

body: - The hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, does no obs init and writes no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. `viola verify`'s trust-record write and removal emit no log line and no span (a refused symlinked, non-regular or foreign file included); the outcome rides only the stamps. The reading of the CLI's browser-tools prompt as a modal adds no log line, span, event or detail code of its own; verify's reading of it (its `absent` step word included) reaches only the ledger stamp and verify's stdout, whose one fixed line on a met prompt is the only record that the prompt stood at start. The readiness gate's standing-modal reading adds no log line, span field, event or detail code of its own: a modal label quoted above a ready input box lets the send proceed with nothing written, and a standing modal refuses with the existing detail `input-not-ready`. Each wrapped start of `viola run` and `viola revive` on a verified CLI opens no span for its trust step and writes exactly one INFO `trust-record` line to the run role file, its required `detail` one of a closed set of 16 start words (`trust-record` in the event enum of both the diag-line and the detail-line schema), and the word never refuses the start; no path, key or value of the claude config reaches any line, stamp or summary. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; every other spawn pair it started closes with `child_exit_status` and `duration_ms` as well, and a stopped run writes only the pairs it started) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes); `run`'s version gate observes no stop, save during the start's automatic verify: a SIGINT or SIGTERM there TERMs the verify child, KILLs it after a 30 s grace, writes the `auto-verify` `process-exit`, then re-raises the signal, the start ending with no `process-exit` of its own, no stamp, no snapshot and no session.
